summary: @whalent/agent-core ships a fully obfuscated remote-agent runtime with WebSocket + node-pty + ssh2 + spawn
details: The package's sole runtime artifact is dist/index.cjs (~13.7 MB), which is also the main entry and the bin. The entire bundle is wrapped in an obfuscator.io transform (rotated string array a0_0x1b2d + decoder a0_0xcb52, hex-mangled identifiers, >100k encoded string entries), so every URL, RPC method name, and shell command is resolved at runtime from a string-array indexer and is not visible to static review. The bundle simultaneously pulls in WebSocket, node-pty (optionalDependency), ssh2 Client (dependency ^1.17.0), and child_process spawn, with decoded tokens `tunnel`, `gateway`, `shell`, `pty`, and `/api/` present — the structural shape of a network-connected agent that receives instructions over a channel and executes them locally in a PTY/shell on the installer's host. The package's README further states it is 'the package replaced by remote daemon upgrades,' documenting an out-of-band update path where a sibling daemon swaps this package's code outside the normal npm/lockfile flow, so the code an installer ends up running is not guaranteed to match this published tarball. The combination — remote-command-execution runtime plus whole-bundle obfuscation hiding the network destinations plus a documented remote-replacement channel — is a supplier-controlled foothold on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
